data.title: Carrier Change Authentication Correlation
data.description: Detects a carrier or SIM change event immediately followed by an authentication attempt on a banking platform. SIM swap attacks involve social engineering or insider compromise at a mobile carrier to port the victim's phone number to an attacker-controlled SIM, after which the attacker uses SMS-based MFA to access accounts. The tight temporal correlation between carrier change and login is the key indicator.

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Carrier Change Authentication Correlation")`
`comment("Aggregation that cannot be expressed in Sigma")`
`comment("Original condition: selection_carrier_change | followed_by selection_auth on phone_number within 120m")`
index=flame_telecom sourcetype=flame:identity_management
(event_type="sim_swap" OR event_type="carrier_change" OR event_type="number_port")
status="completed"
event_type="login_attempt"
mfa_method="sms"
mfa_result="success"
| transaction phone_number maxspan=120m
| where eventcount >= 2
`comment("Sequential correlation across stages")`

falsepositives: Legitimate users who switch carriers and immediately log in to their banking apps
Planned device upgrades where users authenticate on new hardware right after activation
